verdicts.trueWording: "unreliability" as an intricate, hyperrational puzzle, not epistemic uncertainty
verdicts.note: RogerB, 8:50 AM May 8 2015, confirmed on raw page: "it has basically nothing to do with unresolvable ambiguity or genuine epistemic uncertainty... it's 'unreliability' as a kind of intricate, hyperrational trick or puzzle for readers, who assemble based on careful cluing the truth that the narrator doesn't know." Quote exact; both limbs (disputes ambiguity reading; puzzle assembled from cluing) supported.

verdicts.trueWording: revealing how horrible he is through what slips through his narration
verdicts.note: Pseudoephedrine, 12:29 PM May 8 2015: "Severian is a bad guy... revealing how horrible he is through what still manages to slip through his narration." Quote exact. Page says "his narration"; the claim's "his own narration" is a paraphrase outside the quoted span, not a distinct limb.

verdicts.trueWording: sincere recorders who fundamentally misunderstood the events of the story
verdicts.note: byanyothername, 9:00 AM May 8 2015: "Some are sincere recorders of the truth they've experienced, but they've fundamentally misunderstood the events of the story." Quote exact (straight apostrophes on page, matching). Claim's "the events they record" tracks "the events of the story".

verdicts.trueWording: even more central than unreliable narration is deliberate frustration of expectations
verdicts.note: straight, 9:11 AM May 8 2015: "The thing Wolfe does that I think is even more central than unreliable narration is the deliberate frustration of expectations." Quote exact; the comparative limb ("more central than unreliable narration") is on the page verbatim.

verdicts.trueWording: Everything archaic to Severian is rendered as Latin.
verdicts.note: Ipsifendus, 8:57 AM May 8 2015. Quote exact, closing the paragraph "About that language..." whose surrounding comment is explicitly about BotNS/Urth, supporting the claim's "in The Book of the New Sun" limb.

verdicts.trueWording: As he has said, "Everything means something, but not everything means very much."
verdicts.note: straight, 9:00 AM May 8 2015 (attribution line "posted by straight at 9:00 AM on May 8, 2015"). Quote exact; "he" is Wolfe in context ("the solution to his puzzles"), supporting the attribution-to-Wolfe limb.

Ipsifendus, 9:25 AM May 8 2015: "Within the first 2 pages of 'Shadow of the Torturer', there's a contradiction... my wife wrote Wolfe a letter... asking about the contradiction. Wolfe replied by writing me directly... and an explanation for the contradiction: Typo." All limbs (letter, first pages of Shadow of the Torturer, typo answer) supported; the letter was sent by his wife, which the claim does not contradict.

verdicts.trueWording: The novella opens traditionally enough—a childhood memory
verdicts.note: iansales post #1, Jun 13 2006. Quote exact (em dash matches). Context paragraph opens "Something is not quite right about the world of 'The Fifth Head Of Cerberus'", so "the novella" is the title novella, supporting that limb.

verdicts.trueWording: three paragraphs later we learn that the narrator's father traded in children
verdicts.note: iansales post #1, same sentence as index 382: "The novella opens traditionally enough—a childhood memory—but three paragraphs later we learn that the narrator's father traded in children." Quote exact including the curly apostrophe.

verdicts.trueWording: excerpts from taped interviews, field journal, transcripts and prison diary, framed by the officer's reading
verdicts.note: iansales post #1: "It consists of excerpts from taped interviews, the field journal, interrogation transcripts and prison diary of Marsch, framed by a narrative describing the military officer reading those documents in order to make a decision on Marsch's incarceration." Quote exact; military officer and incarceration-decision limbs both verbatim.

verdicts.trueWording: figures describe bullet drop; the authorities take this to mean Marsch is an assassin
verdicts.note: iansales post #1: the evidence is "a table of figures in the back of a copy of A Field Guide to the Animals of St Anne... The figures apparently describe the amount of drop in trajectory of a bullet for given ranges, and the authorities take this to mean Marsch is an assassin." Quote exact; field-guide and bullet-drop limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: Clues in the text suggest his surname is Wolfe—the book under 'W' in the library
verdicts.note: iansales post #1: "'The Fifth Head Of Cerberus' is the remembrances of an unnamed narrator. Clues in the text suggest his surname is Wolfe—the description of a book by his father appearing under 'W' in the library:" followed by the block-quoted shelf passage. Quote exact; unnamed-narrator and library-shelf limbs both supported.

verdicts.trueWording: objective outside detail is usually, in my opinion, at the heart of getting to the bottom of things in Wolfe
verdicts.note: felicibusbrevis post #16, Mar 24 2013, written for the Urth list ("I just wrote this little write up for the urth list"); the sentence sits in the "First, my philosophy on Wolfe's stories" paragraph. Quote exact. Only slippage: the page hedges with "usually", which the claim drops; the claim keeps "in his opinion", so no limb is left unsupported.

verdicts.trueWording: that mythic but confusing dream prose... very different than the first part of the novel
verdicts.note: felicibusbrevis post #16: "The style of A Story is something Wolfe is very good at – that mythic but confusing dream prose that channels the savage mind without losing sophistication. It is very different than the first part of the novel". Quote exact. "Embedded aboriginal myth" is supported on the same page by post #1 ('"A Story," by John V. Marsch' is a Sainte Anne aboriginal myth, as transcribed by Marsch).

verdicts.trueWording: just taking things in at face value and failed to catch the significance of what he was alluding to
verdicts.note: Fried Egg, thread "Peace (*SPOILERS*)", post #1, Sep 14 2010. Quote exact; "he" is Wolfe in context ("Wolfe's eloquant prose"), supporting the "what Wolfe was alluding to" limb.
